title: Projective Hom-complex model with its derived evaluation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P^\bullet$ a bounded-above cochain complex of projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and $N^\bullet$ any cochain complex of $R$-modules. Write $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms into $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $D^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,N^\bullet)$, the product total Hom complex of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with $d(f)=d_Nf-(-1)^{|f|}fd_P$. Write $-\otimes_R^L-$ for the left derived total tensor product and $R\operatorname{Hom}_R$ for its right adjoint internal Hom. The canonical comparison
$$Q(D^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QP^\bullet,QN^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism, natural contravariantly in $P^\bullet$ and covariantly in $N^\bullet$. The ordinary direct-sum total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R D^\bullet)$ represents $QP^\bullet\otimes_R^LQ(D^\bullet)$. Under these comparisons the derived evaluation (the counit for $QP^\bullet\otimes_R^L-\dashv R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QP^\bullet,-)$) is represented by the chain map
$$x\otimes f\longmapsto(-1)^{pq}f(x)\in N^{p+q},\qquad x\in P^p,\quad f\in D^q.$$
Here total tensor has differential $d(x\otimes f)=d_Px\otimes f+(-1)^px\otimes d_Df$. No finite-generation assumption on $P^p$ and no boundedness assumption on $N^\bullet$ are imposed.

proof.text: Termwise projectivity implies termwise flatness by Module.Flat.of_projective. Turn the upper support bound into IsStrictlyLE and apply the generic source theorem CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat, passing to the homotopy category with kFlat_quotient_obj_iff. This is the generic theorem underlying lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat; its specialized acyclicity wrapper is unnecessary.

Build the pre- and postcomposition map on module Hom cochains using the cochain differential composition identities. After forgetting to abelian groups, use Mathlib HomComplex.leftHomologyData and CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv in every degree to identify the homology map with postcomposition by the shifted map in the homotopy category. Bounded-above termwise projectivity gives IsKProjective, so Qh_map_bijective makes that postcomposition bijective whenever the map is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence moduleHomComplex(P,-) preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Compare N with its functorial K-injective resolution.

source.place: Tags 0A8H, 0A5W and 0A66; equation cohomology-hom-complex and Lemma RHom-out-of-projective

proof.text: Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_μ_Qh_of_kFlat to the homotopy image of P and arbitrary D. The tensorator of Q is transported from the tensorator of Qh along quotientCompQhIso, with the monoidal quotient tensorator between them; all factors are invertible. This is the canonical tensor comparison, rather than a bare existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YH, derived tensor computed on a K-flat first complex

proof.text: Construct the chain isomorphism from moduleHomComplex P N to the generic internalHomObj P N by multiplying the degree-n, source-degree-p coordinate by (-1)^(pn). The same formula is its inverse; the differential compatibility follows from negOnePow_add and the cochain differential formula. Transpose this chain isomorphism under tensorHomAdjunction to define evaluation, and use the summand formula for internalHomEquiv.symm to obtain exactly (-1)^(pq) f(x). Define the derived comparison as the curry of Q(ev) after the tensorator. For K-injective N, DerivedCategory.isIso_curry_μ_Qh_counit_comp identifies it as an isomorphism. Transport this criterion along quotientCompQhIso and the signed chain isomorphism, using naturality and the explicit tensorator of Q. For general N use preservation of quasi-isomorphisms from step 2 and the K-injective resolution. Uncurrying gives the required counit square.

Check naturality of signed chain evaluation on each total-tensor summand, by tensor extensionality and the explicit coordinate formula for pre- and postcomposition. Curry its localization, using tensorator naturality, to obtain the mixed derived naturality identity. Package the canonical comparison as asIso; its hom is definitionally the constructed curry. These calculations use neither finite generation nor boundedness of N.
